Identity assessment: cached publisher HTML parse is titled Processing the Word Red and Intellectual Performance: Four Replication Attempts, identifies Collabra: Psychology (2020) 6 (1): 3 and DOI 10.1525/collabra.277, matching the neutral replication reference. Exposed author metadata names Carrie Kovacs; the excerpt does not expose the complete author list, so all three authors cannot be independently checked. It contains substantive primary experimental methods/results for Experiments 1–4 and is not merely an abstract or preregistration. The publisher page is captured in excerpts, not all 1944 original web lines. No source PDF was supplied. Matching uses explicit experiment identity, verbal-analogy outcome, population, and primary hypothesis test, not input order or numeric matching. The primary hypothesis test is the independent-samples t-test described in Experiment 1 Statistical Analyses and Experiment 2 Results (printed d = –0.23). The sex-moderation follow-up is explicitly separate (printed d = –0.27); its participant with missing sex information must not silently be removed from the primary color comparison. Arithmetic/roles: 53 red-condition participants + 51 gray-condition participants = 104 participants; mutually exclusive randomized color groups in Experiment 2. N = 104 is also explicitly printed in Table 1; arithmetic corroborates this N and is not inferred from degrees of freedom. Exclusions: No exclusions from the primary color-only comparison are stated in the supplied main-text sections.
